name: Brasada Ranch
label: Brasada Ranch
about_prose: Brasada Ranch sits on 1,800 acres on the flank of Powell Butte, an unincorporated community in Crook County on the high desert plateau between Redmond and Prineville. The site sits above 3,000 feet, high enough that Brasada Canyons, the resort's golf course, plays with Cascade Range views for most of its back nine. The land was ranch country before Crook County approved the master plan in 2005, and the resort opened to guests in 2007. That plan entitles the property for up to 750 single-family home sites plus 300 overnight resort keys spread across the 1,800 acres, and it sets aside 900 of those acres, exactly half, as permanent open space rather than build-out.

The community earned a distinction early. In 2007 Brasada became the first newly constructed resort community in the United States to receive a Gold rating from the U.S. Green Building Council's LEED program. Brasada Canyons, the golf course, opened that same year: 18 holes across five sets of tees, co-designed by Peter Jacobsen and Jim Hardy, with eleven holes routed through canyon terrain. The recognition continued in the years since. Travel and Leisure named Brasada among its Top Resorts in the West every year from 2021 through 2025, and U.S. News and World Report listed it among Oregon's Best Resorts each year from 2022 through 2025.

Day to day, life runs through the club rather than a downtown, since there is not one inside the gates. Guest and member accommodations include 65 Sage Canyon cabins, 16 adults-only Cascade Bungalows, and 8 Ranch House suites. Spa Brasada operates four treatment rooms. The athletic center has tennis and pickleball courts alongside strength and cardio equipment. The pool complex spans a family pool with a seasonal water slide and lazy river, an adults-only pool, and an indoor lap pool. The equestrian center runs guided trail rides on American Quarter horses, and the 900 open acres carry a trail network for hikers and mountain bikers as well. Ranch House Restaurant serves year-round. Range, open seasonally, serves farm-to-table dinners built around Oregon-grown produce, meat, and dairy. Builders including Stone Bridge Homes NW are still active on the remaining lots as the community fills toward its 750-home cap.

Brasada suits a buyer who wants resort amenities and is fine trading a walk to a coffee shop for real distance in exchange. Redmond is a 22-minute drive, Bend around 25, Prineville about 20. Golf, along with most of the amenities, is open to members and resort guests rather than the public. A purchase here comes with two separate obligations instead of one. HOA dues, which vary by lot, fund roads, common areas, and security. A Club membership is required separately, by property covenant, with its own initiation fee and recurring dues that fund the athletic center, golf, spa, and equestrian access, run by an entity distinct from the HOA. The land around the resort is zoned exclusive farm use under Crook County code, the EFU-3, Powell Butte area designation, so working hay and cattle ground border the community rather than more subdivisions. School-age residents fall within Crook County School District, headquartered in Prineville. Crook County High School serves the district, and Powell Butte Community Charter School, the local elementary-level campus, rejoined the district in 2026 after operating on an independent charter for more than 15 years.

Wildfire is part of living on this stretch of high desert. In July 2025 the Highland Fire burned in Crook County a few miles from the resort, and Brasada opened its Rim Rock Riders arena to shelter close to 20 evacuated horses and other livestock while crews cut the fire from 1,500 acres down to 55 percent containment within two days. Crook County Fire and Rescue's Powell Butte station, a few miles away on SW Reif Road, is the closest full-time crew.
